title: Do not trust the first AI answer
hook: AI is useful, but the first answer is usually a draft.
tip: Ask for the answer, then ask the model to check what could be wrong, missing, or risky before you use it.
why: That second pass catches weak logic, missing context, and confident mistakes.
steps: Give the model the real task.
Ask it to review its own answer.

title: Context beats clever prompts
hook: A simple prompt with good context beats a fancy prompt with no background.
tip: Before asking ChatGPT or Claude for help, give it the role, the audience, the current situation, and what good output looks like.
why: The model performs better when it knows what problem it is solving and who the answer is for.
steps: Say what you are working on.
Show one example if you have it.

title: Automate the repeat work first
hook: The best first automation is usually not the flashy one.
tip: Start with the task your team repeats every week: status updates, inbox sorting, lead follow-up, report drafts, or document cleanup.
why: Small repeatable wins build trust faster than one big risky automation project.

title: Use Claude for long documents
hook: For long documents, use AI like a careful reader, not a magic answer machine.
tip: Ask Claude to summarize the document, pull out decisions, list risks, and identify follow-up questions.
why: This turns a long read into a review workflow while keeping you in control of the final judgment.
steps: Ask for risks and missing details.

title: Keep proof before you scale AI
hook: If an AI workflow matters, keep proof of what it did.
tip: Save inputs, outputs, decisions, screenshots, and approvals for important automated work.
why: Proof makes automation safer because you can check what happened when something goes wrong.
